title: Black Flies of the World
subtitle: Identification keys, species pages and terminology for Simuliidae
rank_conventions: Classification of genera and subgenera follows the current World Blackflies inventory (Adler, latest edition in sources.csv). Oriental species-groups follow Takaoka and co-authors (current Thai checklist) unless a newer source says otherwise (log the difference in conflicts.csv). Cytoforms/cytospecies are noted on species pages, not keyed.

home_intro_html:
Black flies (Simuliidae) are small, stout-bodied biting flies whose larvae and pupae live in running water. About 2,400 living species are known worldwide (2,422 in the 2026 World Blackflies inventory). Females of some species transmit Onchocerca volvulus (river blindness) and blood parasites of birds such as Leucocytozoon. Identification uses the adult (female and male), the pupa (gill filaments, cocoon) and the mature larva.

This site brings together published dichotomous keys from around the world, from keys to genera to regional species keys, and updates them with later taxonomic work. The species coverage is currently deepest for Thailand and South-East Asia.
quick_start_html:
• Decide the life stage: adult female, adult male, pupa or mature larva.
  • Unknown genus? Start with a key to genera on the keys page. For Simulium from South-East Asia, start with the Thai checklist keys (Takaoka et al. 2019).
  • Use Step through. At each couplet choose the lead that fits.
  • Read any ⚠ note on the leads you passed: later work may have added or split species.
  • Open the species page: compare the diagnostic notes, conflicting characters and figures.
  • Unsure of a term? See the glossary.
keys_advice_html: Where to start. Keys are grouped by region. For South-East Asian Simulium, start with Takaoka et al. 2019 (subgenera, then species by stage), then check the species-group keys published since. Keys for other regions are added as the papers are obtained.
glossary_intro_html: Terms follow current black fly morphology as used in the keys on this site; where older keys use other terms, both are listed. Thumbnails open the illustrating figure.
